title: NorESM2-DIAM: A coupled model for investigating global and regional climate-economy interactions
Regional Economic Impacts and Emission Responses under Solar Radiation Modification
venue: Environmental Research Letters (forthcoming); NBER Working Paper 35304
abstract: Solar Radiation Modification (SRM) has been proposed as a potential tool to limit increases in global or regional temperatures caused by anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. While previous research has extensively examined the climate system’s response to various SRM strategies, as well as their aggregate economic consequences, the regional distribution of economic impacts has received less attention. In this study, we use NorESM2–DIAM—an Earth System Model coupled to a high-resolution integrated assessment model—to assess the economic impacts, measured in GDP per capita, in an idealised SRM scenario where incoming solar radiation is reduced by 1%. Our results suggest that, relative to a baseline without SRM, most countries experience economic gains under SRM, with only a few countries facing negative impacts. Low-income countries tend to see the largest benefits, reducing global economic inequality relative to the baseline. However, reduced damages and lower inequality are accompanied by higher emissions under SRM, potentially leading to additional adverse effects not captured here. These findings highlight potential trade-offs between economic benefits, reduced inequality, and increased emissions relevant for SRM governance. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.
abstract_zh: 太阳辐射修正（SRM）已被提议作为一种潜在工具，用以限制人为温室气体排放所导致的全球或区域温度上升。尽管以往研究已广泛考察了气候系统对各种SRM策略的响应，以及它们的总体经济后果，但经济影响的区域分布受到的关注较少。在本研究中，我们使用NorESM2–DIAM（一个与高分辨率综合评估模型耦合的地球系统模型），评估在一个理想化SRM情景（入射太阳辐射减少1%）下，以人均GDP衡量的经济影响。我们的结果表明，相对于无SRM的基线，大多数国家在SRM下获得经济收益，只有少数国家面临负面影响。低收入国家往往获得最大收益，相对于基线降低了全球经济不平等。然而，损害减少和不平等降低的同时，SRM下的排放量也更高，这可能导致此处未涵盖的额外不利影响。这些发现凸显了经济收益、减少不平等和增加排放之间的潜在权衡，这与SRM治理相关。NBER工作论文系列的机构订阅者，以及发展中国家的居民，可以在www.nber.org免费下载本文。

title: Quantifying Uncertainty about Global and Regional Economic Impacts of Climate Change
abstract: The economic impacts of climate change are highly uncertain. Two of the most important uncertainties are the sensitivity of the climate system and the so-called damage functions, which relate climate change to economic costs and benefits. Despite broad awareness of these uncertainties, it is unclear which of them is most important, especially at the regional level. Here we construct regional damage functions, based on two different global damage functions, and apply them to two climate models with vastly different climate sensitivities. We find that uncertainty in both climate sensitivity and aggregate economic damages per degree of warming are of similar importance for the global economic impact of climate change, with the decrease in global economic productivity ranging between 4% and 24% by the end of the century under a high-emission scenario. At the regional level, however, the effects of climate change can vary even more substantially, depending both on a region’s initial temperature and the amount of warming it experiences, with some regions gaining in productivity and others losing. The ranges of uncertainty are therefore potentially much larger at a regional level. For example, at the end of the century, under a high-emission scenario, we find that India’s productivity decreases between 13% and 57% and Russia’s increases between 24% and 74%, while Germany’s change in productivity ranges from an increase of 8% to a decrease of 4%. Our findings emphasise the importance of including these uncertainties in estimates of future economic impacts, as they are vital for the resulting impacts and thus policy implications.
abstract_zh: 气候变化的经济影响具有高度不确定性。其中两个最重要的不确定性来源是气候系统的敏感性，以及所谓的损害函数（将气候变化与经济成本和收益相联系）。尽管人们广泛意识到这些不确定性，但哪一种最为重要，尤其是在区域层面，仍不清楚。在此，我们基于两种不同的全球损害函数构建了区域损害函数，并将其应用于两种气候敏感性差异巨大的气候模型。我们发现，气候敏感性和每单位增温的总体经济损害两者的不确定性，对于气候变化的全球经济影响同等重要：在高排放情景下，到本世纪末，全球经济生产率的下降幅度介于4%至24%之间。然而，在区域层面，气候变化的影响可能差异更为悬殊，取决于一个地区的初始温度及其经历的增温幅度，一些地区生产率提高，另一些地区则下降。因此，区域层面的不确定性范围可能要大得多。例如，在高排放情景下，到本世纪末，我们发现印度的生产率下降13%至57%，俄罗斯的生产率上升24%至74%，而德国的生产率变化范围从增长8%到下降4%。我们的研究结果强调，在对未来经济影响的估计中纳入这些不确定性十分重要，因为它们对所产生的影响及由此带来的政策含义至关重要。

title: Climate Change Around the World
abstract: The economic effects of climate change vary across both time and space. To study these effects, this paper builds a global economy-climate model featuring a high degree of geographic resolution. Carbon emissions from the use of energy in production increase the Earth's (average) temperature and local, or regional, temperatures respond more or less sensitively to this increase. Each of the approximately 19,000 regions makes optimal consumption-savings and energy-use decisions as its climate (or regional temperature) and, consequently, its productivity change over time. The relationship between regional temperature and regional productivity has an inverted U-shape, calibrated so that the high-resolution model replicates estimates of aggregate global damages from global warming. At the global level, then, the high-resolution model nests standard one-region economy-climate models, while at the same time it features realistic spatial variation in climate and economic activity. The central result is that the effects of climate change vary dramatically across space---with many regions gaining while others lose---and the global average effects, while negative, are dwarfed quantitatively by the differences across space. A tax on carbon increases average (global) welfare, but there is a large disparity of views on it across regions, with both winners and losers. Climate change also leads to large increases in global inequality, across both regions and countries. These findings vary little as capital markets range from closed (autarky) to open (free capital mobility).
abstract_zh: 气候变化的经济效应随时间和空间而变化。为研究这些效应，本文构建了一个具有高度地理分辨率的全球经济—气候模型。生产中使用能源所产生的碳排放会提高地球的（平均）温度，而局部或区域温度对这一升高的敏感程度各不相同。约19,000个区域中的每一个都根据其气候（或区域温度）以及由此随时间变化的生产率，做出最优的消费—储蓄和能源使用决策。区域温度与区域生产率之间的关系呈倒U形，经过校准，使高分辨率模型能够复现对全球变暖所造成的总体全球损害的估计。因此，在全球层面，高分辨率模型嵌套了标准的单区域经济—气候模型，同时又呈现了气候和经济活动中现实的空间差异。核心结果是，气候变化的影响在空间上差异巨大（许多地区获益，而其他地区受损），全球平均影响虽然为负，但在数量上远小于空间上的差异。对碳征税可以提高全球平均福利，但各地区对此的看法存在巨大分歧，既有受益者也有受损者。气候变化还导致区域之间和国家之间的全球不平等大幅上升。这些发现在资本市场从封闭（自给自足）到开放（资本自由流动）的范围内变化甚微。
